    """Draw a color-2 rectangular border around the non-background marks."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    background = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    points = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] != background]
    if not points:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    r0 = min(r for r, c in points)

def make_grid(h,w,bg,points,color):
    g=[[bg]*w for _ in range(h)]
    for r,c in points:g[r][c]=color
    return g
# Reconstruct the two demonstrations from all non-background cells shown.
d1=make_grid(19,29,4,[(9,4),(9,5),(10,16),(12,9),(13,9),(14,9),(15,4),(15,16)],0)
d2=make_grid(29,24,5,[(0,3),(10,3),(11,10),(25,3),(25,10)],4)
# Confirm all original marks are preserved and every cell on the inferred bounding-box perimeter is 2 unless marked.
def check_border(g,out,marker):
    pts=[(r,c) for r,row in enumerate(g) for c,x in enumerate(row) if x!=marker]
    # marker here is background color, so find changed perimeter bounds from original non-bg pixels
    pts=[(r,c) for r,row in enumerate(g) for c,x in enumerate(row) if x!= (4 if len(g[0])==29 else 5)]
    r0=min(r for r,c in pts);r1=max(r for r,c in pts);c0=min(c for r,c in pts);c1=max(c for r,c in pts)
    for r in range(len(g)):
        for c in range(len(g[0])):
            expected=g[r][c]
            if (r in (r0,r1) and c0<=c<=c1) or (c in (c0,c1) and r0<=r<=r1):
                if g[r][c] in (4,5): expected=2
            if out[r][c]!=expected:return False,(r,c,out[r][c],expected)
    return True,None
